metadata.note: AI-drafted. A native speaker must check every Spanish line, tag and explanation before this is marked verified. Prices in exercises are illustrative, not real market prices.

concepts.mkt.request: Ask for items politely with amounts
concepts.mkt.quantity: Say amounts such as medio kilo

options.text: Necesito comprar mercancía alimenticia de inmediato.
options.why_not: Grammatically fine, but it sounds stiff and never says which items or amounts you want.

options.text: Buenas tardes. Me da medio kilo de papaya y un kilo de plátanos, por favor.

options.why_not: «Dame» is a casual command with no «por favor», which sounds blunt to a vendor you address as usted.

hints: Which reply tells the vendor exactly what you want?
With a vendor you address as usted, a polite request names the items and amounts and ends with the right courtesy word. Avoid casual commands.
questions.explanation: B names the items and amounts and makes a polite request with «Me da…» and «por favor». A is correct Spanish but stiff and vague. C uses the casual command «Dame» with no «por favor», which sounds rude to a vendor you address as usted.

questions.scene: You see apples and want the price per kilo.

options.why_not: A fair question, but it asks whether they have apples, not what they cost.

options.text: ¿A cuánto es el kilo de manzanas?

options.why_not: The right words are there, but small words are missing, so the sentence falls apart.

hints: Do you want to know whether they have apples, or how much they cost?
Look for the complete question about the price per kilo. Small connecting words matter.
questions.explanation: B asks the price per kilo in a natural, complete way. A asks about availability. C leaves out the small words «el» and «de», so it is not a sentence a vendor expects.

questions.scene: You are speaking politely (usted) to the vendor.

options.why_not: «Tienes» goes with tú. The scene says you are speaking politely, with usted.
«Tengo» means I have, but you are asking the vendor, not talking about yourself.

hints: Who has the avocados: you or the vendor?
When you address someone as usted, the verb takes the same form as for él or ella. Check the present tense of Tener.
questions.explanation: Usted takes the third-person form, so «¿Tiene…?» is the polite question. «Tienes» is for someone you call tú, and «Tengo» is what the vendor would say about themselves.

questions.scene: You want half a kilo of apples.
questions.prompt: Me da ______ kilo de manzanas, por favor.

options.why_not: «Media» is feminine, but «kilo» is a masculine word.
«Mitad» is a noun (la mitad de…), so it cannot sit in front of «kilo» the way an adjective does.

hints: Is kilo a masculine or a feminine word?
The missing word describes kilo, so it must agree with it in gender. One option is a noun, not a describing word.
questions.explanation: «Medio» describes «kilo», so it takes the masculine form: medio kilo. «Mitad» is a noun, as in «la mitad de un kilo».

questions.scene: The vendor tells you the price of avocados.

wrong_answer_tags.missed_tens: answer equals the hundreds part only
wrong_answer_tags.ciento_vs_mil: answer is the price with an extra zero, such as 1,020 or 1,200

hints: Split the number into a hundreds part and a tens part.
Say the hundreds word first, then add the value of the tens word.
questions.explanation: Hundreds come first, then tens: ciento veinte is 100 + 20 = 120. «Ciento» is 100; «mil» would be 1,000.

questions.prompt: How much change do you get?
hints: First write down the price you heard.
Change is what you give minus what it costs.
questions.explanation: Change = what you pay minus the price. For example, 500 − 350 = 150: «me dan ciento cincuenta de cambio».
